In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: what is the risk in terms of efficiency of the estimators of the main error component models when the observations are complete for only a subset of the individuals in the original data set?

the following questions: (a) how does the use of incomplete sub-panels affect the estimation of the parameters of the error components’ models; and (b) what is the risk of using incomplete sub-panels instead original ones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss in efficiency is very small if the sample size is not very small.
the loss of efficiency is not very large if only a few individuals are dropped.
, in general, the use of complete individuals in the estimation of the models under consideration does not lead to a substantial improvement of efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of efficiency is very small for most of the models, but it is not negligible for the random coefficients’ models.
the loss of efficiency is not so large, even for small samples, if the missing observations are not correlated with the regressors.
the loss of information due to the omission of the missing observations can be very high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk function can be used as a tool to measure the risk in a specific application.
the use of complete subsamples is not recommended, unless the researcher can afford a large enough subsample.
the risk is higher when the number of individuals is small.
